articles.title: Mike Florio: Aaron Rodgers’ media appearances showcase ‘open disrespect of Mike McCarthy’
articles.summary: After Sunday’s loss to the New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers took to the postgame podium and initially sounded as if he wer...
articles.body:
After Sunday's loss to the New England Patriots , Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers took to the postgame podium and initially sounded as if he were about to say something selfless.

"In a game like today where there wasn't a lot of flow to it, we need to be better, and it starts with me," Rodgers admitted in what seemed to be a rare moment of accountability.

However, as he continued, he masterfully turned it into what might be the perfect summation of who Rodgers has become late in his career, on and off the field.

"…At like, making sure that Mike [McCarthy] knows what's working and what's not working," he continued. "The coaches know, so that we can call stuff that gives us a better chance."

Throwing his coaches under the bus in Week 2 is pretty much what you'd expect from Rodgers at this point. No one thinks they're smarter than everyone else or is better at painting themselves as an aggrieved victim of a system far beyond their control.

For Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio, this presser is part of a larger pattern he's noticed this season involving Rodgers and his head coach. Specifically, how little respect the 42-year-old quarterback appears to have for McCarthy.

"It's only week 2, he's starting to tiptoe back toward the passive-aggressive comments, the likes of which spawned his quote about not wasting your time reading crap like that, because it was back in 2016, '17, right about there, when he was saying things like, There's no energy on the sideline," said Florio, referencing comments Rodgers made when he and McCarthy were both with the Green Bay Packers .

"And I would say, well, who's responsible for that? Who's responsible for instilling energy? It's the head coach. So you're calling out your coach. There's not enough of a fear that you may lose your job if you don't do your job . Well, who's responsible for that? It's the head coach.

"He wants to be able to do the little drive-by with the criticism and then say, 'I'm just telling the truth, man. I'm just trying to help.'

"He's being a little passive-aggressive here about Mike McCarthy, and I'm not surprised it's starting early. Number one, they struggled yesterday. They looked awful yesterday. And number two, we've seen this coming: the open disrespect of Mike McCarthy between the McAfee appearance, where it was verbal diarrhea episode 1, the Cam Hayward podcast appearance, where it was verbal diarrhea episode 2, 3, and 4.

"I'm not surprised that we're at this point after 2 weeks."

As Florio noted, Rodgers returned to The Pat McAfee Show this offseason after the Steelers, under former coach Mike Tomlin, told him they didn't want him making his weekly appearances . Rodgers returned this summer to take victory laps on Dr. Anthony Fauci and his many critics , amongst other things. He also appeared on teammate Cam Heyward's podcast and blasted ESPN and Dianna Russini while also misconstruing his relationship to people in the media .

All of which, when put together, seems to signal that Rodgers is off the chain once more. And the worse things get in Pittsburgh this season, the more he might push on the passive-aggressive press conference and conspiracy-theory podcast pushes.

articles.title: Mikael Granlund named captain 10th captain in Ducks history
articles.summary: Granlund is the second Finnish captain in Ducks history and the ninth Finnish captain in NHL history.
articles.body:
IRVINE, Calif. – After a summer spent locking down the future, many figured the Anaheim Ducks would look to their young stars to fill the vacant captaincy. Instead, they went with a stoic veteran presence, but if the announcement's reaction at practice is any indication, the Ducks have a leader at the helm.

Mikael Granlund was named the 10th captain in Anaheim Ducks history on Tuesday, making the 34-year-old the second Finnish captain in franchise history and the ninth Finnish captain in NHL history.

"It's a big honor, obviously, being the captain of this franchise and for these guys," Granlund said. "I'm really proud of that, and it's an honor."

Granlund follows in the footsteps of fellow countryman and Ducks legend Teemu Selanne , who wore the "C" in 1997-98, and he is just the second active Finnish captain in the NHL, joining Aleksander Barkov of the Florida Panthers .

"When (Selanne) was playing here, he was the biggest star in Finnish hockey, and everybody was watching him," Granlund said. "I feel like the whole Finland was cheering for Anaheim Ducks always. It's obviously a great honor to be a captain of this franchise."

At the end of Anaheim's practice session on Tuesday at Great Park Ice, Ducks coach Joel Quenneville made the announcement to his huddled mass, and Granlund's teammates charged in for bear hugs and helmet taps.

"Couldn't be happier for him," Ryan Poehling said. "Mikael's such a great guy. Easy guy to be around. He just leads by example on and off the ice. He's the epitome of what it should be, and he's a guy that deserves it."

Quenneville echoed the Poehling's sentiment and said it was he and Ducks general manager Pat Verbeek that made the decision, with more credence to Verbeek on the final say.

With Leo Carlsson signing a five-year deal for league-high money in the summer, Jackson LaCombe locking in for eight years last fall and Cutter Gauthier signing for six years just before training camp, conventional wisdom had any of those three guys pegged to lead a Ducks team that made the jump last season into the future.

Quenneville said the team has "some younger guys down the road," and Anaheim will see how that plays out. Carlsson and LaCombe each will be alternate captains again this season along with veterans Alex Killorn and Troy Terry .

"I think everybody should be pushing to absorb some of that leadership, whether they got a letter or not," Quenneville said. "They're part of the group that we're gonna rely on. Last year, they took a big bite out of it and got some good exposure for us. We're encouraging that same type of participation this year."

When it comes to leadership style, Granlund said he was just going to be himself, because there is obviously something in how Granlund carries himself that made Quenneville and Verbeek choose him.

"The way I try to do things, on ice and off the ice, how you prepare for games," Granlund said. "I think that example, that's the main thing. I want to try to do things as good as you can. You want to do everything you can for the team and help the guys around you. So, that's my play. Just being myself."

From the NHL to the Finnish national team, Granlund has had plenty of countrymen to look up to, whether it was longtime Minnesota Wild captain Mikko Koivu or Finnish national team captain Ville Peltonen.

Those Finns set examples for Granlund to follow, which is how he sees himself taking on the "C" in Anaheim.

"Everybody leads a different way," Granlund said, "but at the same time, all everyone tries to do is do his best for the team, and that's what I try to do. It's not about me. It's about the team, how we can make this team play as good as we can and be successful."

articles.title: Lakers Linked to Standout 23-Year-Old PF in Potential Blockbuster NBA Trade
articles.summary: With October getting ready to say hello, many Los Angeles Lakers fans may have already accepted that the team will not, in fact, make a trade for that big fi...
articles.body:
With October getting ready to say hello, many Los Angeles Lakers fans may have already accepted that the team will not, in fact, make a trade for that big fish power forward.

But Lakers reporter Khobi Price of the California Post had already warned that the Lakers, following the Walker Kessler trade, don't have the ammunition to take another big swing.

"The Lakers' tradable draft picks are limited: They own their own 2033 second-round draft pick; they possess a pair of second-round picks from the Wizards in 2031 and 2032 after swapping Deandre Ayton for Jaden Hardy ; and the lone first-round pick they're able to outright swap in a trade is in 2032. Outside of that, their other trade assets are mostly players who could be on expiring contracts if their team options for 2027-28 are declined (such as Hardy and Dalton Knecht )," Price wrote.

Although that is the case, it is not like the Lakers absolutely have no way to make another trade. It seems unlikely that the team makes a move at this juncture of the offseason, but if the Lakers wanted to get aggressive, there is belief that they would have what it takes to acquire a potential impact player.

Lakers to Go After This Young Rising Star?

If you have submerged yourself in Lakers trade speculation at any point during this offseason, you have likely come across at least a dozen names that the Lakers "could" go after. From the P.J. Washingtons all the way to the Kyle Kuzmas of the world, it darn sure feels like at least one player from every team has entered NBA trade rumors involving L.A. Well, add Indiana Pacers big man Jarace Walker to the list. According to Bleacher Report's Eric Pincus, Walker is among the Lakers' top five trade targets .

"At 6'7″, Walker is more of a perimeter scorer than a bruising power forward, but he's athletic and would add additional depth to the Lakers' frontcourt," Pincus wrote. "The Pacers have consistently avoided the luxury tax, so it's surprising the franchise projects to be over this year by as much as $6.4 million. Many competing executives expect the team to trim somewhere ahead of the trade deadline to get under the $200.4 million threshold."

Pincus outlined that any trade involving Walker, the 23-year-old who was selected with the No. 8 pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, could see the Lakers send out a package of up to four players.

"Walker is the most obvious, expendable player at $8.5 million. The Lakers would need to send out, though they may need a third team to take on one of Dalton Knecht, Jaden Hardy, or Jake LaRavia , to help the Pacers avoid the tax."

Would Walker Be a Difference-Maker for L.A.?

Some Lakers may have scoffed the moment they learned Walker is only a measly 6'7". (I stepped into it, didn't I?) L.A. is already short on frontcourt depth, and Walker would help solve that, but he still wouldn't address two concerns for the Lakers: a lack of size and the need for a starting-caliber power forward.

"He was pretty bad in a big role for the Pacers a season ago when it was kind of the, man, we need him to be really good," NBA insider Keith Smith recently said of Walker on the "NBA Front Office" YouTube channel. "And he got every opportunity to show what he can do and just didn't play that well. And that sucks because I was super high on Jarace Walker coming in. I thought he was gonna be a big ball-handling wing that could do a lot of different stuff. It just never really kind of come together for him."

Walker is young and still very-much ascending. Given the Lakers' recent interest in another rising 23-year-old with two-way ability — don't worry, we won't speak his name again around here — perhaps Walker is a player the Lakers would gladly accept.

The Pacers have a bit of a roster crunch of their own and are creeping up toward those apron penalties. But for the Lakers, it feels like they'd only pull the trigger on a Walker trade if the price were truly cheap enough. (Though it would be cool to have two Walkers in that frontcourt … the Walker-Blockers, anyone? Forgive the digression. And the quirky joke.)

articles.title: UTSA coach Jeff Traylor covers ticket costs for UT Health students ahead of early kickoff
articles.summary: Wanting to spur attendance for Saturday's 11 a.m. kickoff against Colorado State, coach Jeff Traylor is offering to buy tickets for UT Health students.
articles.body:
Wanting to ensure UTSA's home field advantage despite an 11 a.m. kickoff's potential impact on attendance, coach Jeff Traylor began sifting through ideas on the fly.

Offering tequila could be a legal issue, and tacos seemed like a logistical challenge, but then he landed on one that seemed feasible.

"I'll pay for the Health students. I'll pay for the first 100 of those guys' tickets," Traylor said. "Whatever it takes, I'll do."

Within a few hours Tuesday, UTSA athletics found a way to make it official, and for more than just the first 100 takers. All students at UT Health San Antonio can claim free tickets for UTSA's game against Colorado State at 11 a.m. Saturday in the Alamodome, courtesy of Traylor.

UTSA and UT Health San Antonio completed their merger last year, but amid a mountain of logistical hurdles, the policy regarding health campus students' access to athletics tickets was slow to come together.

UTSA announced about a week before the Sept. 5 opener that tickets to the game would be free for UT Health students. For the remaining five home games, the health campus students would be allowed to purchase tickets at the student guest price of $11.

Health campus enrollment is estimated at about 4,000, and those students do not pay the athletics fee that is part of tuition for students enrolled at UTSA.

Traylor has led the Roadrunners to a 34-5 record at the Alamodome through his tenure, but this week's game will be just his second home date kicking off at 11 a.m., accommodating a national broadcast on ESPNU.

UTSA has hosted just one 11 a.m. or earlier home kickoff since 2016, beating Memphis 44-36 on Nov. 2, 2024, and the timing had a clear impact on attendance. The announced crowd of 17,198 was the second-lowest turnout since the 2021 season, and the scanned-in ticket count of 8,958 was UTSA's lowest since 2021.

Sitting 2-1 after wins against UTRGV and Texas State and Saturday's loss to Texas , UTSA can post the program's best start since 2021 with a victory this weekend.

"Our kids have played at such a level the first three games that our crowd should understand the importance of us finishing nonconference 3-1," Traylor said. "We have a real chance to be back to a place we have not been here, and going into conference with confidence."

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani on cusp of Dodgers return but in potentially different role
articles.summary: Shohei Ohtani's time on the injured list is almost over
articles.body:
It's almost all systems go for Shohei Ohtani .

After spending the last two weeks on the injured list nursing right arm and left knee injuries, the Dodgers ' two-way star is expected to be activated on Wednesday, when his minimum 15-day stint on the IL will be up.

"Unless I hear otherwise," manager Dave Roberts said, "he'll be in the lineup tomorrow."

The news represents a best-case scenario for the Dodgers and Ohtani, at least relative to where he was at health-wise when he initially went on the IL on Sept. 11 (in a move that was backdated to Sept. 8).

At that point, the slugger was mired in a 6-for-52 slump at the plate . His hopes of returning to pitching this season had been dashed by repeated setbacks in his pitching program . And he had played in just one of the Dodgers' previous seven games as a designated hitter, after finally showing visible signs of pain from the injuries he had played through for much of the season.

Ohtani was always expected to return to the Dodgers. But it was an open question of whether that would happen before the end of the regular season. And it long ago became clear he was unlikely to get back to 100% this year .

Now, however, the Dodgers at least have some hopeful clarity on the eve of the postseason.

Roberts said Ohtani has felt "considerably" better over the course of his IL stint, noting that "if he was a 5 [out of 10 health-wise] before, he's probably an 8 or 9 now."

On Tuesday, Ohtani was set to check the final box of his return-to-play plan, scheduled to go through coach-pitch batting practice in the team's hitting cages and his normal workout regimen in the weight room.

"Given that's probably a light lift today for him," Roberts said, "he should be ready to go tomorrow."

There is still some uncertainty about where Ohtani will slot into the Dodgers' batting order upon his return.

The resurgence of Mookie Betts has given the team another viable option in the leadoff spot — the place Ohtani has hit previously in every game this season.

Roberts said the choice could come down to pitching matchups, hinting that the right-handed-hitting Betts would lead off against left-handed pitchers (including, potentially, Padres southpaw Robbie Ray on Wednesday) and the left-handed-hitting Ohtani would lead off against right-handed pitchers.

He will have five games left in the regular season to prepare for the playoffs and try to rediscover his typical production at the plate.

After missing two weeks with his first IL stint as a Dodger, he is set to return as soon as he was eligible.

articles.title: 10 things we learned at Rockets media day, from Amen Thompson's goals to Steven Adams' GTA VI take
articles.summary: From Amen Thompson's goals to Reed Sheppard's hair and Steven Adams' GTA VI prediction, here are 10 takeaways from Rockets media day.
articles.body:
Entering last season, with Kevin Durant newly added in the mix, the Houston Rockets expected to take big steps forward. But injuries - one to Fred VanVleet before the season started and another to Steven Adams about halfway through - limited Houston to a campaign that ended the same way the previous one did: 52 wins and a first-round playoff exit.

A long offseason - one that featured a measured approach from the Rockets, who retained their young core and Durant - ended Tuesday with the team's media day, a time of optimism with no losses yet on the ledger.

"We're not here to just make the first round," coach Ime Udoka said. "We want to make some real noise."

"I'm definitely more excited than I was going into last season," general manager Rafael Stone said. "I do think the way Fred's injury hit right on the eve of the season, that was hard on everybody, and so maybe I was a little bit more nervous.

"And this year I feel like I know what to expect more from this group, which lends itself to some excitement for me to see what's going on."

After Stone and Udoka, a host of Rockets players spoke about their offseasons and aspirations for the season ahead. Here are the most interesting things they said:

Amen Thompson is already become an exceptional basketball player - an achievement the Houston Rockets rewarded him for by extending him on a five-year, $208 million deal .

But the 23-year-old, who plays every position on the floor save for center, knows his jump shot will remain a point of focus. Thompson, asked about his offseason work, started with a caveat.

"It's gonna sound kinda corny to y'all but just being the best basketball player I could be," He said. " … I know y'all want me to say shooting and all, I focused on that too, but a little bit of everything: Defense, my handle, playcalling, being a better leader and shooting on top of that too."

Thompson did acknowledge that his defense dropped off last season, leading to him not making the All-Defense teams after being a first-team selection in his second season.

"I didn't deserve it last year, honestly, if I'm being real," he said, saying part of him expected to make the team, leading to the slight drop-off in play. "I want to be a premier defender. I want to make those teams every year, so it definitely was motivation, especially [his twin brother] Ausar making it and me not."

2. Kevin Durant reflects on playoff injuries

During last season's playoff series against the Lakers , there was nearly daily speculation on the availability of Kevin Durant. The future Hall of Famer missed Game 1 of the series with a bruised knee he suffered in practice, then played in Game 2, but injured his ankle in the fourth quarter and missed the rest of the series.

More than four months later, Durant says he wasn't particularly close to returning after that Game 2 injury.

"I couldn't play," he said. "It was hard for me to run up and down the court."

Without Durant on the floor, the Rockets still rebounded from a 3-0 series deficit and pushed it to six games before bowing out. In some of those losses, the flaws of the team's younger players were exposed, but Durant says they'll all be better from it.

"I don't think basketball can put you in uncomfortable positions," Durant said. "You're either going to learn from it or not. I think the positions they were put in in the playoffs is exactly what they needed to go through."

3. Fred VanVleet is a full go - but finding his form is still a process

One of Houston's key returning pieces, point guard Fred VanVleet, made it clear Tuesday - exactly a year since he suffered the ACL tear that cost him all of last season- that he expected some level of adjustment as he returned from the injury

His knee does feel different after the injury and there is no substitute for live game repetitions, VanVleet said. But the guard, one of the league's better on-court organizers and minimizers of turnovers, has played 5-on-5 games and is a full go entering training camp.

"I've been progressing nicely. These things don't always go how you want them to go, how you plan them to go … I feel really good," VanVleet said. "It's going to be a process still so I'm sure what you guys see won't be the finished product. … But yeah, considering 12 months ago I wasn't able to walk at this point in the year, I'd say I'm doing pretty good right now."

Alperen Şengün has become a certified star in the NBA, as evidenced by being selected to play in back-to-back All-Star Games, and the 24-year-old, who averaged 20.4 points and 8.9 rebounds per game last season, expects that trend to continue.

"I was an All-Star two times, but that's not enough," he said. "I want to be there every year. I don't even want to think about, 'Am I going to make it or not? ' I just need to play like I'm ready for this, like I know I'm going to go there and that should be everyone's goal."

Şengün spoke a lot about team goals - namely advancing deeper in the playoffs - but he has an extremely lofty goal for himself.

"Every year, expectations get bigger and bigger and that helps you to become a better player," he said "I want to be the best player in this league one day."

Reed Sheppard shocked some folks when he made an appearance earlier this month with bushy long hair flowing out of the back of his baseball cap . There was no hat at media day, so the guard entering his third season in the league, gave everyone the full look, which he says will change before the preseason starts with a trip to China in October.

"I just haven't gotten a haircut yet," Sheppard said. "I don't really know what I'm waiting on. My goal was to go before media day, but as you can tell, that did not happen. Before we go to China, I will have a haircut of some sort, whether it's still long, short, whatever, we'll see, but I'll have a haircut before we leave."

If he does keep his hair long, he says he absolutely will not wear a headband, but was happy to hear the look was creating buzz on social media.

"I kept it long this summer because most of the time I just threw on a hat, but now obviously you can't wear a hat when you play basketball. I wish I could," he said. "We'll see what happens, but I'm glad some of the people out there liked it."

6. Steven Adams still working his way back

A lot has been made of Fred VanVleet's return from his ACL injury, but Steven Adams' presence will be just as key. As one of the strongest players in the league and most efficient rebounders, Adams' presence was sorely missed when he went out with an ankle injury last January after playing just 32 games.

Adams is about eight months removed from ankle surgery and is back on the court, but getting back to where he was is still a work in progress.

"I've still got to take my time with it," Adams said. "It's one thing to just get back from the injury, but getting back to an NBA level is a different ask."

Adams went into great detail comparing his ankle injury to the knee injury that kept him out the entire 2024-25 season, saying the knee injury took much longer to return from, but the ankle injury is more mental because it's the landing point for every step and the rest of the leg absorbs the constant impact.

"There's a lot of bones down there, mate, it's a bit complicated," he said.

Adams also offered a prediction: Performance across sports leagues, not just for players but also coaches and scouts, will dip in November before rebounding (hopefully) in December.

His reasoning: "GTA is dropping," Adams said, referring to the long-awaited release of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI.

Tari Eason focused his offseason on getting in shape, ballhandling, the base of his shot and adding more arc to his jumpers.

"This offseason was probably the most diligent I've ever been, the most focused I've ever been with my attention to detail," he said.

"New money," he said, referring to the five-year, $80 million extension he signed with the Rockets after testing restricted free agency in the summer. Part of that is him trying to validate the contract but part of it, Eason said, is going through the offseason with a clear mind and healthy body.

"It's amazing," Eason said about the extension. "I'm happy to be here. It's a blessing to be able to spend my time with the Rockets here. I got drafted here, so I'm very happy about it."

At just 23 years old, Jabari Smith Jr ., will be the second-youngest player in the Rockets' regular rotation, but as he enters Year 5 in the league, he's ready to take on more of a leadership role.

Even at his age, Smith, who was the third overall pick in the 2022 draft, is the third-longest tenured Rockets player on the roster behind only Alperen Şengün and Jae'Sean Tate.

"I definitely want to be more vocal," Smith said. "I definitely want to be somebody where my voice is heard. I don't want to call myself old, but I've seen a little bit now being in the playoffs two years and being in Ime's system for a little bit now. I feel like I know what he wants and what the team wants and I think it's on me to use my voice a little bit more and be a little more vocal and take on that leadership role more. I think it will help everybody, so I'm ready to take on that challenge."

10. Marcus Smart happy to be on Durant's team

Marcus Smart is happy he doesn't have to guard Kevin Durant anymore.

"I get to be on the other side of him taking the shots and not taking the shots over me," Smart said. "It's just tough, his ability to make shots - it doesn't matter who's there and it also doesn't help that he's close to 7-foot and I'm close to 6-foot, right?"

Now, Smart said, his job is just to pass Durant the ball and watch him do what he does best: Shoot.

articles.summary: Bad news for the Philadelphia Flyers in their second preseason matchup. Goaltender Dan Vladar exited Tuesday’s game against the Boston […]
articles.body:
Bad news for the Philadelphia Flyers in their second preseason matchup. Goaltender Dan Vladar exited Tuesday's game against the Boston Bruins with an apparent injury.

Aleksei Kolosov replaced Vladar at the 13:31 mark of the first period.

It's unclear what injury the goaltender may have sustained, but based on video, it looks like it may have been something with his upper body. Specifically, his blocker side.

It's unclear if Vladar will return to action on Tuesday, because as of this moment, Kolosov remains in goal. Given the nature of it being a preseason game, it would make little sense to have Vladar come back into action.

If the injury exit is more than precautionary, it would be a crushing blow to the Flyers early this season. Vladar was very clearly the team MVP during the 2025-26 season.

If injured, it makes the offseason acquisition of Joseph Woll all the more important.

An update will be provided on Vladar when one is given.

articles.title: Ronald Acuña Jr. exits game with apparent leg injury, is day-to-day
articles.summary: Well this is certainly concerning.
articles.body:
Welp, this was just about the absolute last thing that anybody wanted to see with the Postseason on the horizon. With two outs in the third inning and a full-count, Ronald Acuña Jr. fouled one off of his lower leg on one of the spots that wasn't protected by padding. He was in obvious pain and the trainer attended to him while manager Walt Weiss went out to check on him as well. After a bit of a lengthy examination, Acuña limped off of the field and Brewer Hicklen came on to finish the at-bat.

Needless to say, losing Acuña for the Postseason would be a huge development and not in a good way, either. It would also stink for Acuña since he's been doing so well in recent weeks and I'd imagine that on a personal level, he'd love to contribute to any type of deep Postseason run that the Braves could make.

For now, here's hoping that this is just a substitution being made with a precautionary eye towards the Postseason and not anything serious. We'll see what happens, though.

UPDATE [8:33 p.m. ET]: The Braves have possted on social media that the X-rays on Acuña's lower leg were negative and that he's currently listed as being day-to-day. That's a big sigh of relief.

articles.title: DeVonta Smith stands two catches from Eagles franchise history
articles.summary: DeVonta Smith needs two receptions against Chicago to become the fastest player in Eagles history to reach 400 career catches
articles.body:
DeVonta Smith is two receptions away from becoming the fastest player in Philadelphia Eagles history to reach 400.

Smith's 10-catch performance against the Tennessee Titans increased his regular-season total to 398 receptions through 82 games. According to Reuben Frank of NBC Sports Philadelphia via team record books, if he catches at least two passes against the Chicago Bears , Smith will reach the milestone in his 83rd game. Zach Ertz currently holds the franchise mark after making his 400th reception during his 86th game with Philadelphia .

Smith's latest performance also moved him higher on another significant Eagles list. His 117-yard afternoon against Tennessee marked the 16th 100-yard receiving game of his career, the seventh-highest total in franchise history.

Pete Retzlaff holds the Eagles record with 23. A.J. Brown has 22, while Harold Carmichael, Mike Quick and DeSean Jackson each recorded 21. Tommy McDonald finished with 17. Smith could tie McDonald with one more 100-yard performance and is only seven away from matching Retzlaff.

The numbers reflect the consistency Smith has provided since Philadelphia selected him in the first round of the 2021 NFL draft. He has produced as a featured receiver, secondary option and postseason performer while becoming one of Jalen Hurts ' most trusted targets. That connection was decisive against Tennessee. Smith caught four passes for 38 yards during the winning drive, including a 19-yard reception that placed Philadelphia at the Titans' 3-yard line.

Smith's next two catches will make history. His current pace suggests he'll do much more.

articles.title: Braves playoff worst nightmare may have come true after Ronald Acuna Jr. exits game
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves are a week away from their WildCard playoff series. Ronald Acuna Jr. has left the game after sustaining an injury, marking a real concern...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves have had an up-and-down year with Ronald Acuña Jr. , as he has struggled with injuries this season. However, over the past month, he has been on a tear.

Acuña, when healthy, is one of the best players in the entire league. At the beginning of September, he was on an absolute tear.

"Ronald Acuña Jr. is heating up in September, and it's exactly what the Atlanta Braves have been waiting for. Acuña has missed 53 games this season due to injury, and outside of a solid May in which he hit .286 with five home runs, his offensive season has been underwhelming. That's what makes the calendar flipping to September such a welcome sight. Through the first four games of the month, Acuña is 8-for-18 with two homers, five RBIs and four runs scored," SI's Roman Janeiro wrote.

The only concerning thing is that, as it stands, Atlanta is questioning whether or not to extend him. Acuña is open to it, but the Braves are still figuring it out.

"Now Acuña, I'm sure, would welcome talks for an extension because he'd had so many injuries, but I just don't see it happening. I do see him, in two years, becoming a free agent," MLB insider Ken Rosenthal said.

The Braves are gearing up for the playoffs, and Acuña is going to be a huge factor. However, disaster struck on Tuesday night when the MVP fouled a ball off his leg and had to exit the game.

"Ronald Acuña Jr. has been taken out of the game after he took a swing and the ball ricocheted off his leg. We'll have more updates when they become available," The Athletic's Jesus Cano posted.

As of now, there is no update on the severity of his injury. It did look pretty painful, but with the playoffs starting in a week, Acuña may not see the field much even if he is able to play.

The 28-year-old is going to be a big part of the Braves team that wants to make it back to another World Series. Acuña potentially not playing in the playoffs gives Atlanta a nightmare it does not want to face. This could be a worst-case scenario at the absolute worst time.

articles.title: Shohei Ohtani Set for Dodgers Return With Leadoff Role in Question
articles.summary: Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani is set to be activated on Wednesday, September 23rd, after missing a few weeks with right arm soreness.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers supersta r Shohei Ohtani is set to be activated on Wednesday, September 23rd, after missing a few weeks with right arm soreness.

According to manager Dave Roberts, Ohtani will return immediately to the starting lineup on Wednesday and is set to be the leadoff hitter, though the skipper is weighing whether to split time with Mookie Betts depending on the matchup.

Ohtani had been slumping badly as the leadoff hitter, while Mookie Betts has had one of the best months of hitting on the team.

The Japanese star will likely have to prove he can hit before fully taking over the leadoff role.

Why Shohei Ohtani was put on the injured list

Ohtani's swing and plate approach looked off over the last handful of games, and the Dodgers saw enough to sit him.

His left knee injury and right bicep discomfort both stem from his pitching work.

The Dodgers initially benched Ohtani without putting him on the injured list, but after he returned for a game and still looked compromised, they officially placed him on the IL.

What has Ohtani been doing while on the IL

Ohtani rested for the first half of his 15-day IL stint, but has started swinging the bat again more recently.

As he has continued to progress, Ohtani has improved enough to be activated.

Additionally, for the Dodgers' recent road series, he has not traveled, opting to stay in Los Angeles and work at home.

These next few games will show where he is and what he can deliver at the plate, and they'll let him shake off the rust before the postseason.

By all accounts, he should be much improved, since he said rest would help most. Now, that theory will be tested.

articles.title: ‘I can start my senior career confidently’: Anahat Singh on the Asian Games and what comes next
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Anahat Singh's first reaction after winning the World Junior Squash Championship was not about what the title might do to her profile.This was her las.
articles.body: Anahat Singh's first reaction after winning the World Junior Squash Championship was not about what the title might do to her profile.This was her last year in the junior circuit, and after years of playing squash, she finally had the title she wanted before moving fully into senior competition.“I think it's a good way to end my junior career, I'd say, because it's my last year playing juniors as well. I'm going to be turning 19 before I can play any other junior event so I think it's just a good way,” Anahat told Timesofindia.com.“I've been playing squash for 10 years, and it's a good note to end it and start my senior career so I can start it confidently and in a good way as well.”The timing is crucial because the Asian Games are already here. Anahat is the third seed in the women's singles draw at Aichi-Nagoya, with a first-round bye. World No. 6 Satomi Watanabe is the second seed; defending champion Sivasangari Subramaniam is the top seed.And the singles gold also carries an Olympic consequence as well. The women's singles winner gets a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Games, where squash will make its Olympic debut.Anahat already has experience of having played at the Asian Games once. At Hangzhou, three years back, she won bronze in the women's team event and another bronze in mixed doubles. This time she is in the singles draw and understands the importance of the continental event.The Asian Games comes next“The Asian Games is way more important. And it's a pivotal point in my career as well for me to reach the LA 2028. And I think just working more towards that and focusing on one thing at a time, and not focusing on what's there in two years and just taking it step by step.” she said.Her parents have been telling her the same thing since she started playing squash.“I mean, I think that's one thing that my parents have always taught me since I've started playing squash that once an event is over, OK, you enjoy it for like a few more days. And then once it's done, you focus on the next event.”The junior title has also changed the expectations around her.“I mean, of course, it [expectations] would definitely change it, but I still think there's so much for me to achieve.“It's still just the junior stage, I still have to go into the seniors, and I think this event is just something that gives me more confidence going into the seniors knowing that, you know, like I've mentioned before that I'm ending juniors in a very good note and I can start off my new chapter really well and, you know, continue to do well and hopefully be a world champion in the senior stage as well and not just in the juniors.”There had been something to build on before the World Junior Championship. Hong Kong, last December, was one of those moments.“I went for a tournament in Hong Kong, one of my first senior tournaments, and I played a girl from Belgium, ranked inside the top 20, and I had a 3-1 with her. I think that was one of the moments where I realized that, okay, I had one of the best matches of my career till now and I had so much fun while I was on court and this is something that I can really imagine myself doing for the next 10-15 years and even longer possibly.”“So I think just that match specifically was something that really turned my mentality around where I was like, I really need to push and I can, you know, I really want to play more events like this. I want to play against more of the top players and I think I'm capable of, you know, playing good matches like this and even possibly beating some of them.”“I think that happened last year in December and I think I've come a long way since then.”The people behind the playerThe move into senior squash has brought Anahat into a different kind of training environment, with Gregory Gaultier and Saurav Ghosal around her.Gaultier was a world No. 1 and a World Champion; Ghosal has reached the top 10 and is a pioneer when it comes to squash in India. Both have spent years dealing with the sort of situations Anahat is now beginning to encounter on the senior circuit.“I think just being around them and being in that environment, they've both been at the top of the game. Greg was world number one, world champion and Saurav has been top 10 in the world. So they've both experienced a lot more than I have in their careers.”“And I think just the fact that they've experienced it all is just something that helps me out for the future as well, because, you know, I'm prepared for it,” she said.The difference is also showing up in her results against senior players.“I'd say mainly just the amount I've learned playing with the seniors. As I mentioned before, I'd have maybe 3-1s or like close games with the senior players in the top 10 and top 20. But, you know, just being able to play against them and being able to win those matches is something that I've learned, especially from Greg and Saurav, because they've played a huge role in just making me learn, you know, the psychological part of it, the mental part of it and even the physical part.”The physical side is now one of her priorities.“Yeah, I'd say my physical aspect, I've not, I'm still only 18 and my parents always said that stay away from the gym as much as you can because you're still young.”“So you have a lot of time to work and go into the gym. And I think, yeah, now I've realized that now that I'm going into the seniors as well, it's very, very important for me to, you know, go and improve my physical aspect, the fitness part of it.”She has been working on that for the past year, although travelling makes it difficult to maintain.“I've started working on it in the last one year, but it does get really hard to, you know, be, to maintain it when I'm traveling a lot.”A recent visit to the Red Bull Athlete Performance Center gave her a clearer idea of what needed work.“I mean, it was a very new experience for me. It was, I got to do so many different testing. And like I said, I need to need to work a bit more on my physicality aspect.”“So I think just the testing helps me see, you know, the details of what I really need to work towards. And it's not just an overview of everything. I can see exactly what I need to work and what I need to do.”PV Sindhu, her sister and the family behind herThe changes have not been confined to training. Anahat has been watching athletes around her and learning from people she followed long before she was playing squash at this level.PV Sindhu was one of them. While training at Siri Fort in Delhi, Anahat remembers watching Sindhu play there from around the age of five.“I think one of my first memories from sport and from badminton is of her and watching her matches.”She has since seen Sindhu at the Commonwealth Games Village and Asian Games Village.“So I think just getting to see her from so early on and I've also seen her a few times, you know, at the Commonwealth Games Village and the Asian Games Village and just learning and seeing what she's like off the court and, you know, I think she's an inspiration to so many people.”“She’s achieved so many great things for Indian sport and, you know, she's someone who's inspired me in so many ways and, I mean, hopefully I can take on some of the things that she's done for the country and, you know, try to somehow reach the same level as her in squash as well.”There was also someone closer to home. Anahat's older sister had played squash, so the sport was already part of the family when Anahat started playing.Her parents then took on much of what came with that career - the coaching, the travel and everything around the tournaments that Anahat herself did not have to worry about.“I wouldn't be where I am without my parents.They've done everything for me to get me to the stage. I'm still only 18. So everything that happens behind the scenes regarding the coaching, the traveling, there's nothing to do with me. It's all them handling it.”“They travel with me for all of my events. They're there for some of my practice sessions. They're watching me play.” So I think just having that kind of support is just something that's brought me to this level and I wouldn't, I would definitely not be where I am if it wasn't for them.”India's history, Anahat's singles opportunityIndia's squash record at the Asian Games has been built largely through team events and a handful of individual medal runs.The country has won 18 squash medals at the Games so far - three gold, four silver and 11 bronze. Five of those came in Hangzhou, including two golds. Joshna Chinappa, competing at her seventh Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, has five Games medals, including an individual women's singles bronze from Jakarta-Palembang in 2018.For Anahat, the next few years will bring more tournaments, bigger opponents and, potentially, more medals. But her own definition of how those years will go is a little different.“For me, I'd say if I'm satisfied with the way I'm playing and what I'm producing, I think that would be successful for me, whether it's winning 100 medals or winning one very important medal.“And if I'm happy with what I've done and if I'm satisfied with what I've done for myself, for my family, for my coaches, my country, and if I've done enough for them, I think that is what success would mean. And if it's through medals, then yeah, great.”“But if it's also through what you've achieved and what you've worked on and how much you've improved in the last few years, that is also considered the same thing.”For now, Anahat is sticking to the method she described herself.“...focusing on one thing at a time, and not focusing on what's there in two years and just taking it step by step.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
